text:
It was Robert F. Kennedy who famously noted that " Each time a person stands up for 
an ideal or acts to improve the lot of others... he sends forth a tiny ripple of hope. " In 
the context of our work at the Leduc Center for Civic Engagement, these words serve as 
more than just an inspiration—they are our operational blueprint. And they are framed 
in our office as a reminder for all. This past year, we have witnessed thousands of these 
individual ripples: a student mentoring a local youth, a faculty member researching 
sustainable urban solutions, and community partners coming together to address food 
insecurity. Each act, though small in isolation, represents a profound commitment to 
the belief that our world can be made better through intentional, individual effort. 
However, the true power of Kennedy’s vision lies in what happens when these ripples 
meet. He spoke of how they " build a current which can sweep down the mightiest walls 
of oppression and resistance. " Our coordinated collective effort is transformational. 
Over the last twelve months, the Leduc Center has focused on bridging these individual 
efforts to create a unified force for change. By providing the resources, training, and 
platforms necessary for civic discourse, we have transformed disparate acts of service 
into a cohesive movement. This annual report details how those individual "ripples" 
have converged into a powerful current of progress that is reshaping our campus and 
the surrounding community. 
As we look toward the coming year, we invite you to reflect on your own contribution to 
this movement. Whether you are a student just beginning your journey in service or a 
long-time supporter of our mission, your actions are the vital energy behind everything 
we achieve. We do not expect every person to "bend history itself," but as this report 
demonstrates, each of us has the power to change a small portion of events. Together, 
we will continue to stand up for our shared 
ideals, ensuring that the ripples of hope 
we start today become the transformative 
currents of tomorrow. Together we 
continue to build a foundation for a more 
just, equitable, and participatory future. 
Yours in Service, 
Matthew H. Roy, Ph.D. 
Assistant Vice Chancellor 
for Civic Engagement
